_comment: Body app, Fuel tab. The basics page (protein, creatine, diet and weight), how to log calories by photo in MacroFactor, editable water and protein-shake defaults for the tap counters, the 'less of' counter, and supplement notes on NAC, caffeine and L-theanine. Research behind the numbers, kept off the screen: protein, ISSN position stand, Jager et al. 2017, pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28642676; creatine, NIH ODS, ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/ExerciseAndAthleticPerformance-Consumer, and ISSN, Kreider et al. 2017, pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28615996; weight loss pace, CDC, cdc.gov/healthy-weight-growth/losing-weight; calorie target, NIDDK Body Weight Planner, niddk.nih.gov/bwp; water, National Academies 2004 report on dietary intake levels for water, salt and potassium; caffeine, FDA, 'Spilling the Beans', fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/spilling-beans-how-much-caffeine-too-much; L-theanine, Owen et al. 2008, pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18681988, and Giesbrecht et al. 2010, pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21040626; NAC, Al Alaili, PLoS One 2026, pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42853821. General information only, never medical advice.
doctor_line: Not medical advice. Ask your doctor before any supplement, especially if you're pregnant, take medication, or have a heart, kidney or liver condition.

sections.title: Protein
sections.how_much: 0.65 to 0.9 grams per pound of body weight, every day.
sections.when: Spread it across meals, 20 to 40 grams each.

sections.title: Creatine
sections.how_much: 3 to 5 grams of creatine monohydrate a day.
sections.when: Any time. Every day, rest days included.
sections.what_it_does: Fuels short, hard efforts like lifting and sprinting.
sections.heads_up: Expect a couple of pounds of water weight early on.

sections.title: Diet and weight
sections.how_much: Eat a little less than you burn to lose. A little more to gain. Aim for 1 to 2 pounds a week.
sections.how: Start with the NIH Body Weight Planner. Log for two weeks. Adjust by 100 to 200 calories a day.
simple_rules: Fruit or vegetables at most meals.

defaults._comment: Starting values for the Water and Protein tap counters. Every one is editable by the reader and saved on their phone or account.

water.why: A round starting goal. Drink more on gym days and hot days.

protein_shake.why: One shake covers a big piece of your protein.

less_of.what: A counter you set yourself. Nothing is preset.

fields.label: What you'll do instead
fields.hint: A walk, a book, a call

stephen_example.name: Scrolling after dinner
stephen_example.swap: A walk, a book, a call.

items.name: Caffeine
items.what: The stimulant in coffee, tea and energy drinks.
items.how_much: The FDA cites 400 milligrams a day for most healthy adults. That's two to three 12-ounce coffees.
items.watch_for: Jitters, racing heart, upset stomach, bad sleep.

items.name: L-theanine
items.what: An amino acid in tea, sold as a capsule. Often paired with caffeine.
items.how_much: Studies used about 100 milligrams with 50 milligrams of caffeine.
items.evidence: Two small studies found better focus and alertness.

items.name: NAC (N-acetylcysteine)
items.what: A form of the amino acid cysteine. A medicine for decades, also sold as a supplement.
items.evidence: Lots of research, uneven quality. Not in standard guidelines for everyday use.
